unit.title: Reading CVC Words and Simple Sentences

lesson.title: Meeting a New Vowel: Short I
lesson.subject: ela

contentBlocks.text: Yesterday you read short-A words like cat and hat. Today we meet a new vowel sound: short I, like in 'sit' and 'pin'.

The short I sound is quick and small: ih. Say it together and notice your mouth barely opens. Now blend some CVC words with short I: s-i-t, sit. p-i-n, pin. h-i-t, hit. Practice reading each one, then try comparing a short-A word to a short-I word: cat vs. sit — notice how just changing the vowel changes the whole word.
You now know two vowel sounds: short A and short I. Tomorrow we'll practice reading words with BOTH vowels mixed together.

objectives: Produce the short I vowel sound and read short-I CVC words (sit, pin, hit)
Compare short-A and short-I words, noticing how changing the vowel changes the word
materialsNeeded: Optional: letter cards for I, P, N
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Model the short I sound: quick and small, 'ih'.
2. Introduce any new letters needed (P, N) if not already known.
3. Blend sit, pin, hit together, slowly then faster.
4. Compare a short-A word (cat) to a short-I word (sit) — same pattern, different vowel, different word.
5. Move to the worksheet: read and trace each short-I word.
6. Close by asking the child to spot the vowel in each word they read today.
differentiationTips: Struggling: keep comparing back to yesterday's short-A words as an anchor before fully committing short I to memory
Ready for more: ask the child to change one letter in a short-I word to make a new word (sit -> sip, pin -> pit)
For a child who mixes up short A and short I, use exaggerated mouth-shape modeling (wide open for A, barely open for I)
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a reading and tracing-practice activity — check that the child can blend and read each short-I CVC word.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Introducing a second short vowel builds the vowel-flexibility Grade 1 readers need to decode a much wider range of CVC words, directly extending yesterday's short-A foundation.

generationData.instructions: Read each word by blending its sounds, trace it, then write it once more on your own.
